newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese enterprises outperform Hong Kong market.
newsitem.headline: Chinese enterprises outperform Hong Kong market.

text.p: The H shares of Hong Kong-listed Chinese enterprises have outperformed the market due to demand for laggards after a recent rally in quality stocks and China-related shares, brokers said on Tuesday.
"H shares outperformed the market on demand for laggards, especially those quality undervalued H shares," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises index was up 53.06 points or 6.28 percent to 898.30 at midday on Tuesday, compared with gains in the blue-chip Hang Seng Index of 169.39 points or 1.29 percent to 13,313.62.
"It's about time for H shares following the recent rally in red chips and B shares," Mak said.

Analysts say red chips, or Hong Kong-based China-focused companies, especially those having strong ties with Chinese authorities, are increasingly favoured by investors eager to tap into China's economic growth.
The B shares of Chinese enterprises are listed and traded on mainland stock exchanges and are for foreign investors only.
"Sentiment towards H shares improved a bit recently," said a sales director at a regional brokerage.
"Investors are likely to become more selective in picking up the stocks following the rise in the overall (H-share) sector," she said. "Focus is likely to be on those having good fundamentals."
The H shares of Qingling Motors Co Ltd were up HK$0.45 or 13.04 percent to HK$3.90 at midday on Tuesday.
Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd was up HK$0.14 or 12.28 percent to HK$12.28 and Guangshen Railway Co Ltd gained HK$0.20 to HK$3.325.
